Building a tower with stacked boxes needs robust 2D physics, rotation, friction, stacking. Writing a custom rigid body engine with SAT and sequential impulses is doable and safer offline. But polished game physics is hard. Could vendor matter-js from npm? Check network availability. We can `npm pack matter-js` if network. But static deployment may not include node_modules. Game design:

Theme: "Tower Tumble" or "Fort Friends". Cute pastel sky, rolling hills, wooden fort, egg target.

Core loop:
1. BUILD phase (Player 1 / You): budget of 12 blocks. Choose block material: wood (cheap, 1), stone (2, heavy/strong), glass (1, fragile but long?) — maybe plank sizes: small cube, long plank, column. Grid-snapped drag-and-drop with snapping to grid or free placement? Grid-based building is easier and cleaner for stacking: place blocks on a 20px grid within the build zone; physics turns on in attack phase. Free-form placement with grid snap makes towers stable.

Better building UX: inventory of pieces: wood plank (wide), wood column (tall), stone block, glass pane. Drag from palette onto the build area, snapped to a grid. Show ghost preview + cost. Egg is the "treasure" that friend tries to hit.

2. ATTACK phase: Friend (AI or Player 2) gets 3 birds. Aim with drag from slingshot (pull back, release), trajectories, destructive impacts. Damage model: blocks have HP; high-speed impacts reduce HP; birds have mass and knockback. Egg loses HP if hit/falls. If egg destroyed -> attacker wins; if birds run out -> builder wins.

Score: builder scores for egg remaining HP + blocks standing. Attack scores for damage.

For solo experience, Player vs AI attacker is essential. Also add "Friend mode" hotseart? Could add mode toggle "VS AI" and "2 players". AI attack aim: compute physics-ish trajectory to target egg with slight error; maybe choose pull vector and simulate? Simple: solve ballistic arc with gravity to target, adjust for slingshot anchor and power, add random error based on wave.
